Sources indicate that another Mashable Choice titleholder, the fresh Oura Ring 5 has a slimmer design that makes it more comfortable to wear for long periods of time — yet it still lasts up to seven days per charge. According to Mangino, who's used to wearing an Apple Watch, its jewelry-like look and fit make it the ultimate everyday wearable. Its "exceptional" activity tracking (her words) and useful health insights are just the icing on the cake. Read our full review of the Oura Ring 5.

Pokémon fever is running high for the legendary franchise's 30th anniversary. So, whether you're shopping for a 5-year-old or a nostalgic millennial who’s still a kid at heart, expect Pokémon gifts to be in very high demand for Christmas 2026.

Select brands have collaborated with the IP to release various special-edition products, including Adidas and Beats. We're also huge fans of the adorable Lego Smart Play Pokémon sets. Our advice: grab available items ASAP or bookmark product pages to watch for restocks. You can thank us later.

Recent findings suggest that A fitting gift for any modern bookworm is an e-reader. We've also named the new Amazon Kindles some of our favorite Christmas gift ideas of the year (keep scrolling), but there are other options we love. Another Mashable favorite, the Kobo Libra Colour, lets readers highlight passages in color and makes comic books and graphic novels more engaging. We also love the new reMarkable Paper Pure, a powerhouse e-ink writing tablet that doubles as an e-reader for PDF and ePub files, without any ads or pop-ups. Read more about the best e-readers.

We think the TCL QM6K is the best TV for most people. Former senior shopping reporter Leah Stodart deemed it "the quintessential beginner fancy TV": a nice QLED model with adequate brightness, deep blacks, great color, and a high-enough refresh rate for gaming, but a reasonable price tag. (Every size is usually on sale for well under $1,000 — even the huge 85-incher.) It's primo "for casual home theater purposes," Stodart wrote. Read our full review of the TCL QM6K.

Industry observers note that there are plenty of ways to trick out a newly introduced iPhone. Moft’s cult-favorite, origami-styled phone stand is a great tech stocking stuffer that magnetically snaps onto the back of a phone and folds into three viewing positions. A built-in sleeve holds up to two cards, giving you some on-the-go and on-the-desk swagger. It's compatible with all MagSafe iPhones (and Android devices with magnets), making it one of the best Christmas gifts under $50.

Birdbuddy's smart feeders are super popular Christmas gifts, and the brand just came out with two latest models: the Birdbuddy Nook and Birdbuddy Home. Henschel tested them and prefers the Home because it has a larger seed reservoir and two built-in solar panels. However, the small, affordable Nook is "ideal for tight spaces like balconies and patios," she remarked. Both feeders are super easy to set up and have an upgraded, scratch-resistant camera with AI-powered bird species recognition.

Industry observers note that this fall, Apple came out with its first-ever smart display, the HomeView. Parents can use it for FaceTime calls, sending messages, listening to music, catching up on highlights, and answering questions or controlling other smart home devices via Siri AI. It also doubles as a digital picture frame. (Like Amazon's Echo Show devices, it's basically an all-in-one hub.) Up to six people can set up their own profiles on it, so it's well-suited for bigger households. Read our first impressions of the Apple HomeView.

If your family is spread out in different states, then a digital picture frame lets mom, dad, or your grandparents keep track of the entire family — no matter where they are. Everyone in the family can add new pictures remotely, and their picture frames will show a slideshow of your latest adventures.

Classic board games stir up sweet family memories. WS Games leans into that with its vintage-inspired collection. Battleship, Candy Land, Clue, Monopoly, Risk, Scrabble, and numerous other classics receive a bookshelf-worthy makeover. Each edition has a hardcover-style design and interior storage for the pieces, so it can sit proudly on a bookshelf instead of being tucked away in a closet.

According to recent reports, what are the best Christmas gifts for men, you might be wondering? We have a whole separate list of gift ideas for guys, but to make things quick, Breeo's USA-made fire pits rock.

They're smokeless, capable of providing hours of entertainment, and available in stainless or corten steel finishes, the latter of which develops a rustic patina over time. Breeo also sells a lot of accessories for its fire pits, including a Heavy Duty Fire Poker — another one of our go-to unique gifts for men. It has the feel and heft of a harpoon, and it can shift logs around until you have the perfect blaze.

According to recent reports, the best robot vacuum and mop combos can take two chores off Mom and Dad's plates — a priceless Christmas gift, if you ask us. Out of all the new models that Stodart tested this year, she thought the Eufy C28 was the best affordable option. Additionally, its "AI-powered small obstacle avoidance will reliably avoid toys, cords, laundry, or whatever else you didn't have time to tidy up," Stodart said. Read our full review of the Eufy Robot Vacuum C28.

There is something so luxurious about a brand-latest set of bath towels that all match and feel wonderful. It's like a warm hug each time you get out of the shower. Brooklinen's are particularly loved by our staff — tech editor Werth stated, "I firmly believe that Brooklinen's Super-Plush towels are the best towels in the world, period. They're insanely fluffy yet dry faster than you expect.".

It has been revealed that whiskey drinkers have specific tastes. Unless you know exactly what they want, then let Flaviar’s 2026 advent calendar do the choosing. This year’s edition hosts 24 great-tasting whiskies from around the globe. Each box comes with guided stories, tasting notes, and digital content for every reveal. Pricewise, it costs less than many Pappy Van Winkle releases.

For the right kind of dad (or a very cool mom), it's a gift he'll really appreciate — just be sure to give it to him at Thanksgiving so he has time to savor each day's release.

Sources indicate that there's a non-zero chance that your parents, like so many other homeowners with a little disposable income, have procured a 12-foot skeleton from the Home Depot within the last few years. (It can talk now, in case you didn't hear.) If that's the case, this custom Santa costume will give them an excuse to leave it up through the holidays. We won't tell their HOA if you won't.

Industry observers note that apple’s flagship headphones have never been cheap, but thanks to Black Friday sales, the holiday shopping season is your chance to score a pair at a discount — or hope someone especially generous puts them under the tree. This time of year, they're often marked down as low as $449.

Beyond the price, the Apple AirPods Max 2 are an upgrade from the original, boasting the H2 chipset for enhanced active noise cancellation and integrated smart audio features such as Adaptive Audio and Conversational Awareness. They also support true lossless audio over USB-C connection to hear more detail and nuance from Apple Music tracks. Read our full review of the Apple AirPods Max 2.

Industry observers note that the travel-friendly Anker Prime Power Bank packs enough power to charge an entire laptop on the go, and it's an incredibly practical gift for anyone with a lot of devices to keep charged (i.e. everyone). Wherever you are, this portable power bank can charge a laptop, a handheld gaming console, and a smartphone — all at the same time.

DJI is best known for its drones, but don't sleep on its creator-friendly cameras and microphones, either. The DJI Mic Mini has a cult following among TikTokkers, and it's a personal favorite of our own reporters. Compatible with both iPhones and Androids (plus a host of cameras), these are the exact microphones that the Mashable social team uses at events such as VidCon. Read our full review of the DJI Mic Mini.

The Mashable Choice Award-winning Insta360 Luna Ultra is a upcoming 8K gimbal camera with dual lenses and a detachable two-inch touchscreen for remote operation. Mashable assistant editor Amanda Yeo thought the latter was a really neat feature: It "turns the Luna Ultra from a nifty handheld camera into a super flexible vlogging tool that can capture more angles with ease, and is particularly attractive for solo shooting," she wrote. It's a solid investment for any aspiring or professional creator. Read our full review of the Insta360 Luna Ultra.

The Octobuddy is a colorful silicone suction mount that lets you stick your phone onto any smooth surface for impromptu videos. TikTok-obsessed teens will undoubtedly appreciate its simple design that makes filming GRWM videos and dance challenges way easier. We frequently see the Octobuddy mentioned in our In My Bag creator interview series.

According to recent reports, the latest installment in the Grand Theft Auto series has been 13 years in the making, and we're not being dramatic when we say it's the most anticipated video game of all time. Its story will follow a criminal couple through the streets and swamps of Leonida, a fictional version of Florida. If its soundtrack is anything to go by, it'll be a banger. If you preorder GTA 6 before launch day on Nov. 19, your giftee will get bonus vehicle, weapon, and character cosmetics.

Recent findings suggest that the secret ingredient to some of the very best gifts of 2026? Pure, unadulterated nostalgia.

For its latest remake, Nintendo modernized 1998's Ocarina of Time with better visuals and physics, upcoming voice lines, a fresh score, and free camera controls. According to Mashable tech reporter Alex Perry, who got to play the game for an hour at a press preview event, it's a thoughtful update of a stone-cold classic. "It isn't the same as a brand new Zelda for [the Nintendo] Switch 2," he wrote, "but it'll do until the time comes." It's out Nov. 5, and you can preorder it now.

According to recent reports, clips of Pokopia gameplay went massively viral this spring, and for good reason. It's "Pokémon meets Minecraft, with a delightfully goofy premise and the potential for lots of town-building fun to be had either by yourself or with a group of friends via online play," Perry wrote. It's such a good game that a lot of people upgraded to the Nintendo Switch 2 just to play it. Read Mashable's full review of Pokémon Pokopia.

Perry called the Nintendo Switch 2 "a fabulous follow-up to an all-time legend." It won a Mashable Choice Award for its upgraded system software and great online social features. Perry also loved its new magnetic Joy-Con 2s, which are bigger and more satisfying to use than the original Switch's controllers. We think it's the best handheld gaming console to buy in 2026, even after a price hike. Read our full review of the Nintendo Switch 2.

Lego had retro gamers tweaking last year with its awesome Game Boy replica. For its encore, the iconic toy maker jumped a few gaming generations ahead, creating this Sony PlayStation set in celebration of the system’s 30th anniversary. It’s an awesome recreation of the original and features customizable details paying homage to two classic launch titles: Ape Escape and Gran Turismo. One look is enough to bring back 32-bit-era memories.

The sixth installment in Sarah J. Maas' hit romantasy series, A Court of Thorns and Roses, arrived this October, and no self-respecting BookTok member should miss it. If you really want to earn brownie points with your bibliophilic giftee, preorder them a copy of the next book, which is set for release in January. Both are available in hardcover, paperback, audiobook, and Kindle e-book formats.

Sources indicate that amazon redesigned its Kindle e-readers for 2026 with fun new colors (ube! seaglass green!) and thinner, lighter form factors. After testing the updated base model, Mashable's Mangino crowned it the best budget e-reader. "What truly makes it stand out is just how lightweight it is," she wrote — at six inches and half a pound, it's excellent for travel. Read our full review of the new Amazon Kindle.

Industry observers note that however, if you have a little more wiggle room in your gifting budget, Mangino thinks the newly introduced Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best Kindle overall: It's waterproof, longer-lasting, and equipped with an adjustable warm light. Read our full review of the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition.

In a recent development, psst: Don't forget to remove the Kindle lockscreen ads before you gift. To quote our tech editor, "it's borderline rude" not to.

Sources indicate that amazon's first page turner, the Kindle Click, "will level up your cozy evenings spent reading," remarked Mangino, and it's a must-have for the BookTok set. It lets you turn the pages of a Kindle or adjust its brightness when you're snug under the covers of your fuzziest blanket. (It's compatible with models from 2024 onward.) Unlike other page-turners we've tried, it works via Bluetooth. Read our full review of the Amazon Kindle Click.

A gooseneck stand is a "luxury" for any regular e-reader user because it situates the device "within reading distance without any arm fatigue," Mangino said. Based on her testing, this Magipea model works nicely with both Kindle and Kobo models. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Sources indicate that trivia night at the local bar is fun, but hosting one at home can be even better. Hitster is an icebreaker that gets everyone working together to identify hit songs from the past century. Scan a card to play a track, then guess the year it was released. Themed editions — including All American, Guilty Pleasures, and Latino —broaden playability and let you tailor the music to your manufacturer.

It has been revealed that multiple Mashable editors and writers swear by Loop's earplugs, which look like jewelry, fit comfortably in most people's ears, and make a unique stocking stuffer. The Loop Experience 2 are great for regular concert- and music festival-goers; Mashable's Henschel even wore them to a Beyoncé show. "I could hear Beyoncé and her band perfectly, but the din of the stadium was almost completely suppressed," she wrote. They come in a range of color options, including some limited-edition metallic variants designed in partnership with Harry Styles.

This spring, Sony launched some latest Bluetooth record players for the first time in seven years. Henschel tried the entry-level PS-LX3BT model and called it "a stylish turntable with idiot-proof plug-and-play functionality." She pointed out that it has a USB-B port in the back, which you can use to rip vinyl tracks onto a laptop. If your partner collects vinyl, this is one of those Christmas gift ideas they'll appreciate for years to come. Read our full review of the Sony PS-LX3BT.

CDs are the latest retro tech to have a resurgence among Gen Z. Tracking down a cool old CD player on eBay will earn you a lot of cred, but if you don't want to go through the trouble, this see-through model from Retradisc looks really, really cool. It works with wired or wireless headphones, and best of all, it doesn't cost as much as Sony's new gold-plated Walkman.

Technics continues to make a strong impression in the wireless audio market. When it comes to hi-fi headphones, the fresh EAH-A1000 are a sonic stunner that put many category leaders to shame. They crush the AirPods Max 2 in most areas and rival the Sony WH-1000XM6 sound quality, while also outlasting both competitors in playtime (up to 45 hours per charge) and multi-point pairing. Plus, the elegant craftsmanship is a 10/10. Every audiophile should have this at the top of their wish list this year.

Recent findings suggest that sonos has long been a go-to for WiFi speakers, but JBL’s newly introduced Cove Series is a true competitor that offers a compelling wireless audio experience at a more attainable price. If you have someone on your shopping list who loves music, the Cove speaker will fill up their bedroom, living room, or back patio with big sound.

Plus, it even offers automatic self-tuning, AI Sound Boost technology that optimizes audio for listening environments, and hands-free Alexa voice control.

In a recent development, choosing a signature scent for your hubby isn’t as easy as picking out a video game; you need to know their olfactory preferences. If you’re unsure what they like — or shopping for someone especially particular — let them decide with one of Fulton & Roark’s discovery sets. The variety gives them a chance to explore different scents and narrow down their next go-to fragrance. (Pro tip: We like Palmetto and Ghost Trees.).

Harry’s has something for every man’s mug. Guys who prefer a clean-shaven look can reach for the brand’s shaving kit, which includes the popular Truman handle with secure grip and multiple five-blade cartridges that deliver close shaves. No-shave November devotees can keep their mane well-kempt with the beard wash and conditioning spray bundle.

Every well-groomed gentleman deserves a luxury electric shaver in his life. The Panasonic Arc5 Pro is our pick for its comfortable, close shaves and flexible head, which is designed to improve cutting performance. It works for both wet and dry shaving, and the built-in pop-up trimmer provides seamless control and navigation to clean up edges around the neckline.

We think the Mashable Choice Award-winning Shark CryoGlow is the best red light mask you can buy right now (and one of the best Christmas gifts for women). It provides more complete coverage than other masks from brands like OmniLux or CurrentBody, and each bulb can emit red, blue, or near-infrared light.

Former senior shopping reporter Leah Stodart was convinced that the CryoGlow’s bacteria-killing blue light setting is what finally cleared a year’s worth of her relentless adult acne. Some cooling under-eye pads complete this luxurious self-care device. Read our full review of the Shark CryoGlow.

Several Mashable staffers use Shark's FlexStyle multi-styler on a regular basis. (Mangino did her wedding hair with it!) It costs half as much as Dyson's iconic Airwrap but works just as well, if not better. It supports a ton of different attachments and has a unique twisting base that functions like a regular hair dryer on its own. Read our full review of the Shark FlexStyle.

The Playground is a cubic gaming console designed for playing family-friendly games with motion controls — no need for a traditional gamepad. Perry described it as "a spiritual successor to the old Xbox Kinect." If this is the first time you're hearing of it, get with the program: It managed to outsell the PlayStation 5 on Black Friday 2025, and was difficult to find in stock during the holiday season last year. If you strategy on gifting it within the coming weeks, we'd recommend adding it to your cart ASAP.

Fascinatingly, this squishy little toy is one of the hottest products of 2026. People have stormed stores and waited hours in line to buy them, and there's even a reselling market for them. Mashable's Mangino bought some before the hype and said they "promptly became coveted fidgets among our friends for their pleasing, pliable feel.".

Sources indicate that like wired earbuds, CD players, and other items from your childhood, Pokémon cards are so incredibly back — and dare we say, bigger than ever. The Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration Elite Trainer Box is a giftable bundle that includes 9 booster packs and plenty of other goodies. Amazon is also selling it on an invite-only basis; try your luck because it's well under market price, as of this writing.

Sources indicate that routine can give children structure and help them feel more secure. The Skylight Buddy guides kids through mornings, afternoons, and bedtime, while helping them develop healthy habits and independence. They can add and check off chores, events, and tasks. This digital calendar also functions as an alarm clock and nightlight, signaling wake-up and sleep times. Personalization features help families reinforce goals and daily commitments.

Industry observers note that we recently named the Toniebox 2 one of Mashable's Gifts of the Year in our guide to the top gifts for kids. The kid-famous Toniebox is a favorite of the moms and dads on the Mashable team. Whether you're shopping for your own child or trying to earn a reputation as the cool aunt or uncle, kids and parents alike love these screen-free storytelling devices.

Sources indicate that if your tyke already has a Toniebox, they can always use more Tonies — the little figures you put on top of the device to activate a fresh storytime. Bluey and Pokémon Tonies joined the party this year.

Industry observers note that another Mashable Gift of the Year winner, this portable screen-free audio player is a hit with the three kiddos of Nicole Cammorata, Mashable's director of special projects. "Compatible cards power up everything from chapter books and shorter stories to music and learning-based content," she wrote. For an incredibly sweet personalized gift, you can have grandparents, siblings, or friends record custom audio messages on blank Yoto cards.

In a recent development, don't overthink (or overspend) trying to think of the perfect Christmas gifts for kids. Keep it simple and combine two things kids love — Bluey and slime. This slimy sand adds a bit more texture to the average slime, letting kids mold it in new ways. Even better, you can pick it up for under $15, and still have the best gift under the tree.

According to recent reports, gifting a pair of the best Beats headphones is a sure bet for any fashion-forward music lover. Fans of over-ear headphones will appreciate the modular Beats 360, which features a customizable design with swappable ear cushions, IPX4 sweat resistance, pleasant sound, and strong ANC. True wireless conformists can utilize the sporty Powerbeats Pro 2 for exercise and leisure; the revamped earhook design is optimized for comfort and sound performance.

Looking for the best gifts under $100? The Camp Snap 2 is one of our top picks. This screenless digital camera has six built-in filters and super simple controls. To transfer its photos to your phone, all you need is a USB-C cable. Mangino brought a Camp Snap 2 on her Grecian honeymoon this past summer, "and now I have the sweetest photos to look back on," she noted. Read our full review of the Camp Snap 2.

It has been revealed that the merchandising gods are working their magic this holiday season in anticipation of the biggest MCU film yet: Avengers: Doomsday. Funko Pop has a tempting lineup of Marvel collectibles, including multiple versions of Doctor Doom, beloved X-Men characters, and a 10-inch jumbo Sentinel. Steve Rogers, Thor, Shang-Chi, and several other familiar faces round out the collection.

Industry observers note that if your teenager is allowed to watch TV in their room, upgrade their older set to the Mashable Choice Award-winning Hisense DécoTV. The 32-inch model "is compact enough to fit just about anywhere and simplistically chic enough to fit in with just about any decor," stated Stodart. It'll be perfect for their college dorm room when the time comes. As a bonus, it costs much less than Samsung's smallest The Frame TV. Read our full review of the Hisense DécoTV.

No one's too old for Play-Doh anymore: This summer, the modeling clay brand released its first-ever collection of adult craft kits, Blooms by Play-Doh. Each one comes with colorful, scented Play-Doh sticks that they can press and shape into a pretty floral bouquet, plus finishing spray and a clear vase. For crafty types who have grown bored of Lego's Botanical builds, this is one of our favorite Christmas gift ideas.

In a recent development, the upcoming Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8 is the best flip phone we've tested this year, and Mashable's Werth especially recommends it "for a stylish, on-trend young person." It's easy to hold in one hand, durable, and available in an extremely cute purpley-pink color. And while its camera setup isn't wildly impressive, it does take a mean selfie. Read our full review of the Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8.

In a recent development, retro tech is having another moment. Last year, cassette players were everywhere; this year, Bluetooth CD players are joining the old-school wave (there are two in this gift guide). They’re a fun pick for Gen Alpha teens who love iPods, disposable cameras, and DVDs, and you can pair it with their favorite artists' latest albums.

The Fosi Audio Merak works as a portable and desktop CD player, with modern extras including Bluetooth, USB drive playback, and one-touch CD ripping.

The best Christmas gift for a hostess with the mostest is a Ninja Slushi Twist. It makes delicious frozen cocktails, slushies, and milkshakes just as well as the original Ninja Slushi, but now it works faster, picks settings for you, and adds a second mixing canister. That's right: Two flavors at once, baby. It's "just plain fun, and will make your home the go-to for your friend group," said Stodart, who gave it a Mashable Choice Award. Read our full review of the Ninja SLUSHi Twist.

Recent findings suggest that bless the tea sipper in your family with this flavorful collection of 18 premium blends that bring winter warmth and wellness. These loose-leaf teas come in plant-based sachets and are sourced from small-scale farmers. The assortment includes multiple varieties of black, green, mint, oolong, and white teas.

Recent findings suggest that the viral Ninja Crispi and the newly introduced Cosori Iconic have both earned the Mashable staff's collective seal of approval. Why those air fryers, you might ask? Not only do they crisp up food nicely, but they're free of plastics and forever chemicals. The compact Crispi is ideal for cooking single-serve meals and meal-prepping; its glass containers come with lids for storing your leftovers. The Cosori is a sleeker stainless steel model with a bigger basket and handy smart controls. Read our full review of the Cosori Iconic.

It has been revealed that A digital dosing cup with a precision scale for weighing beans before grinding is the gift every coffee drinker didn’t think they needed until now. The Subminimal Subscale powers on promptly and features a hidden LED display for easy-to-read measurements. It can handle hot and cold liquids, and its minimalist design complements modern kitchen counters.

Industry observers note that the new Series 12 is the best smartwatch for most iPhone consumers, in our opinion. It has a faster processor, pretty new ceramic finish options, and an improved heart sensor array. Mashable senior editor Stan Schroeder has been testing it this fall, and he said the latter is "the star of the show" because it "allows for far more frequent measurements." It also "opens the door for new apps such as Readiness and an overhauled Vitals app," he added.

We loved the Google Fitbit Air when we first tested it, and love it even more after the latest update, which supports automatic detection for up to 100 sports and tracks blood pressure trends. It excels as both a fitness tracker and sleep tracker, making it a superb gift that athletes won’t ever take off. Not to mention it’s way more affordable than the Apple Watch Series 12, Oura Ring 5, and Whoop MG. Read our full review of the Fitbit Air.

Almost everyone on Mashable's shopping team owns an Owala FreeSip, which Mangino dubbed the "best water bottle ever." The 24-ounce insulated stainless steel bottle is designed to accommodate both sipping (via straw) and good ol' fashioned gulp when tipped back. For athletes, college students, teenagers, or anyone who drinks water, we think a colorful Owala is one of the best Christmas gifts under $50. Read our full review of the Owala FreeSip.

Mashable tech reporter Matt Binder, a self-proclaimed "longtime soccer dad," tested the new XbotGo Falcon sports tracking camera for an entire youth soccer season this year. His verdict: It's "a smart pick for parents and coaches." Its footage is sharp, you can monitor it in real time from your smartphone, and it works with nine different sports (soon to be 12). It's a bit of a splurge, but unlike a lot of the competition, it doesn't require a subscription. Read our full review of the XbotGo Falcon.

Tossing the football is a holiday tradition for many sports-loving households. This year, rifle this waterproof football into your dad’s chest. Dime Labs cleverly designed its footballs with silicone grip strips for better handling, and a woven microfiber cover to survive the wettest conditions. It comes in two sizes – 10.5 inches and 8.5 inches – with the smaller version well-suited to kids practicing their quarterback skills.

It's a cooler. It's a boombox. It's both! We love the Igloo KoolTunes for its old-school design and surprisingly good audio quality. While it lacks deep bass, it offers clear, balanced sound and can get quite loud. "It's not a gimmick, but a fun fusion of summer party gear," stated Mashable's Henschel. Read our full review of the Igloo KoolTunes.

The latest Shark ChillPill is another Mashable Gift of the Year winner. It's a powerful portable fan that stands out for its swappable misting and cooling plate attachments, long battery life, and fun colorways. (Justin Bieber's SKYLRK brand teamed up with Shark for a limited-edition "Heat" variant, which is long sold out.) It came in clutch for Mangino on some of the hottest days of the summer. Read our full review of the Shark ChillPill.

The LifeStraw is a Black Friday classic that always goes on sale around the holidays, which also makes it a perfect stocking stuffer for people who love camping and the great outdoors. You can stick one end of this straw into virtually any water source — no matter how gross — and clean, filtered water comes out the other end.

Portable Bluetooth speakers are crowd-pleasing gifts for just about anyone, from teenagers to parents, siblings, and friends. This year, we're loving the all-newly introduced Tribit StormBox Micro 3. It produces satisfying sound in a compact design, is fully waterproof, and comes in multiple standout colorways. Tribit’s speaker is travel-friendly, with a magnetic snap that can latch onto fridge doors or bike handles.

Simply put, Yeti's stainless steel Rambler tumblers are crowd-pleasers. They're dishwasher-safe, incredibly durable, condensation-resistant, and available in a huge rainbow of colors and patterns. Pro tip: For a very affordable personalized Christmas gift, you can customize a Rambler with your own text, graphics, and logos on the Yeti website.

Power stations can come in handy in lots of unexpected situations. From camping at music festivals to charging up your phone in an emergency blackout, these lightweight and portable devices keep you on the grid. Bluetti makes some of our favorite power stations, and the Elite 30 V2 is a good starter model.

It has been revealed that the AirFly Pro is a cult-favorite Bluetooth adapter that makes seatback screens on older planes compatible with wireless headphones. After using it on round-trip flights between Chicago and London, Henschel mentioned she'd "never fly without it again." The newer AirFly Pro 2 has simpler controls, improved sound quality, and pairs faster. Read our full review of the Twelve South AirFly Pro.

Industry observers note that traveling abroad this winter? Take this handy adapter along. Anker’s latest travel charger works with outlets in nearly every country and can charge up to four devices at once. The voltage detection system monitors voltage, power output, and temperature in real time. All readings and charging statuses are displayed on the LCD screen.

Travel jewelry cases are both thoughtful and practical, and we like this one in particular. The velvet box comes in a few different colors, and it ensures your wife, girlfriend, or daughter's favorite rings, necklaces, and earrings never get misplaced when she's away from home. If you're hunting for one of the best Christmas gifts for women under $25, look no further.

It has been revealed that cushy ANC headphones are a non-negotiable for long travel days, and lead shopping reporter Bethany Allard thinks the latest Bose QuietComforts are the best mid-range option for flying. When she wore them on a plane, "I heard minimal engine hum and was able to completely tune out conversations from my fellow passengers," she wrote. "I also never felt the need to remove the headphones due to wear fatigue." Read our full review of the Bose QuietComfort headphones (2nd Gen).

According to recent reports, nori’s garment steamers are a lifesaver for business travelers and fashion professionals. The Cloud Max makes de-wrinkling clothes a breeze, using gentle vacuum suction to pull fabric taut for smoother results. Anti-spit technology prevents leaks and water spots, and the steamer’s portable design fits comfortably in any travel bag.

A weekender bag bridges the gap between a backpack and a suitcase. It should hold a few outfits, toiletries, and an extra pair of shoes for a two- or three-day trip. Quince’s Voyage bag fits the bill with a dedicated shoe compartment, multiple pockets, and a padded shoulder strap. It’s presently on sale for half of its original price, while supplies last.

Still looking for more great Christmas gift ideas? Check out even more of our favorite gifts to give in 2026:.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Soon, your alarms, timers, and phone calls will be less disruptive on iPhone Duo.

With today’s iOS 27.3 developer beta 2, iPhone Duo gained a upcoming feature: Unlock with Front Camera. This lets you unlock your iPhone Duo in a similar fashion to Face ID, but using the front selfie camera, rather than Face ID’s TrueDepth 3D camera system. But, Face ID is more than just unlocking: it also provides Attention Aware features.

Attention Aware features, which were first introduced with iPhone X, check for when you’re looking at the phone before performing certain actions:.

iPhone will check for attention before dimming the display, expanding a notification when locked, or lowering the volume of some alerts.

Sources indicate that previously, Attention Aware features required Face ID, but iOS 27.3 extends it to iPhone Duo. Like the latest face unlock feature, Attention Aware features only work when using the outer display. However, the face unlock feature does not have to be set up to use the Attention Aware features.

Industry observers note that after updating to iOS 27.3, the features should be automatically enabled. You can enable or disable the feature in Settings → Accessibility → Face Recognition & Attention. You can also enable Haptic on Successful Unlock there, just like an iPhone with Face ID.

In my experience, Attention Aware features will lower the volume of alarms, timers, and incoming calls when your iPhone is already unlocked. It also will prevent the display from dimming and locking while you are actively looking at it. Finally, it will expand and show notification content on the Lock Screen after unlocking with the latest face unlock feature.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Moon has reached its First Quarter phase, with half of its visible surface now illuminated. Over the coming days, the Moon will keep getting bigger a we move towards the Full Moon.

It has been revealed that as of Tuesday, Nov. 17, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the First Quarter phase, with 48% of its surface visible.

Sources indicate that if you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Vaporum, Fecunditatis, and Crisium. With binoculars, you'll also see the Endymion Crater, Posidonius Crater, and the Mare Nectaris. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 17 landing spot and the Linne Crater.

The next Full Moon will take place on November 24.

According to NASA, the Moon goes through a complete cycle of phases roughly every 29.5 days. As it orbits Earth, the portion of its sunlit surface visible to us changes, giving rise to the different lunar phases. The cycle begins with a Upcoming Moon, progresses to a Full Moon, and then gradually returns to a New Moon before starting all over again.

Newly introduced Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

Sources indicate that waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere).

Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

#1001. Oobah Butler Can Sell You Anything—If You’re a Rich Idiot

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1564 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

Oobah Butler Can Sell You Anything—If You’re a Rich Idiot

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1564 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You’d think that Oobah Butler would have run out of schemes by now.
  • The gonzo British documentarian’s repertoire includes creating an entirely fake restaurant—The Shed at Dulwich—and getting it to the top spot on London’s Tripadvisor; selling bottles of Amazon drivers’ urine on the ecommerce site; and convincing venture capitalists to give him $1 million.
  • But as his new HBO show, Oobah: Scams for a Better Tomorrow, makes perfectly clear, Butler still has plenty of tricks up his sleeve—and it’s a delight to watch them unfold.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You’d think that Oobah Butler would have run out of schemes by now.

The gonzo British documentarian’s repertoire includes creating an entirely fake restaurant—The Shed at Dulwich—and getting it to the top spot on London’s Tripadvisor; selling bottles of Amazon drivers’ urine on the ecommerce site; and convincing venture capitalists to give him $1 million.

But as his new HBO show, Oobah: Scams for a Better Tomorrow, makes perfectly clear, Butler still has plenty of tricks up his sleeve—and it’s a delight to watch them unfold.

The series rolls out November 22. Each of the premier season’s five episodes centers on Butler scamming his way into success in a different industry—wellness, wine, dating, music, and a finale I do not want to spoil—with increasingly outlandish ideas that, somehow, almost no one advises him against.

His shock of bleach-blond hair and appearance of a Victorian ghost notwithstanding, there are undeniable similarities between Butler’s style and that of master of manipulation Nathan Fielder. Both use satire and parody to make social commentaries, and both often divert from their original intends by hyperfocusing on what the average person might consider a tangential detail, carrying these side quests to extreme lengths. But while Fielder has sometimes been criticized for roping unassuming working-class folks into his hijinks, in Butler’s case the joke is almost always on the rich and powerful—and the systems that allow them to prevail.

Butler in the New York weather.

It has been revealed that “The whole show can be reduced to ‘monkey see, monkey do,’” Butler tells me from a coffee shop at the Upcoming York Historical Society in Manhattan, where he’s just ordered a latte with four espresso shots and been recognized from TikTok by a fellow patron. “I just find these bad actors and copy them.”.

Butler’s knack for convincing high-profile—in some cases notorious—executives and tastemakers to appear on camera and earnestly weigh in on his ridiculous plans at times boggles the mind. In the series premiere, he sets out to start a wellness organization that sells the tears of human children as a skin serum, and gets none other than former Theranos chief creative officer Patrick O’Neill to consult on a marketing strategy.

Recent findings suggest that applying his characteristic charm, Butler tells O’Neill he “smashed it” with creating mystique around the scandal-plagued biotech startup, to which O’Neill replies, “Thank you, yeah. I think it’s good to share the knowledge.”.

Butler wearing glasses designed to collect the tears of children.

After briefly expressing hesitancy around the ethical sourcing of the tears, O’Neill begins offering Butler packaging advice: a tear-shaped bottle, and the two discuss the name Lacrimé (“tears” in Italian). “It makes it feel exotic and not necessarily something you’d see from Johnson and Johnson,” O’Neill says, in all seriousness.

Confiding in $1,500-an-hour lawyer Jennifer Keller about how he may have committed fraud with his wellness venture, Butler tells her the industry is “a gold rush of bullshit. And I want in.” She laughs and notes that he sounds “more and more like an American.” It’s all very funny, but as the name of the show hints, there is a Robin Hood quality to Butler’s scamming, in this case exposing the poorly regulated nature of skin care and supplements.

It has been revealed that butler has chosen the Upcoming York Historical Society as our meeting point because he loves history, and New York’s in particular. When he first moved here in February 2024, he started reading Robert Caro’s The Power Broker, a biography of influential urban planner Robert Moses, giving him an understanding of “how power works” in the city. But his itch to move came well before that, when he visited in 2016.

“I just found it so inspiring,” he states, dressed in a maroon velvet shirt, baggy dark jeans, and Salomon sneakers, a Patagonia backpack slung over his shoulders, as we set out for a walk in Central Park. “I got to an age where I just thought, well if I don’t do this now, I probably am not going to do it.”.

Although New York is indeed full of power brokers—and very wealthy ones at that—he notes it’s different from the aristocracy he grew up around in Feckenham, a 700-person “Hobbiton-style village” in the UK.

“I grew up in a lower-class family … I’ve definitely got a bit of a chip on my shoulder about class,” he notes, noting that he’s the youngest of six siblings. “And America, for all of its concerns, there is something amazing about how I see the same guys who really wind me up in the UK—upper-class kind of guys—and the way that they walk the earth and the way they feel and the way they carry themselves. I see them come here and no one gives a shit. Really, truly, no one gives a shit.”.

Butler didn't go to college. He started a band called My Grey Horse in 2010, playing guitar and singing. Around the age of 17, he began writing music reviews, secretly hoping to score his band some coverage. “It was a scam on the go,” he says. But he caught the writing bug, finding it “meditative.” Later, he joined VICE (where I previously worked as a senior reporter) as a freelance video host, making a bunch of documentaries, including the extremely viral one about The Shed. From there, he did several films for the UK’s Channel 4 and cohosted MTV’s Catfish UK.

Industry observers note that “It changed my life and was absolutely the right thing to do. I wouldn't have been able to afford to move here if I hadn't done Catfish,” he says.

Though he tells me he’s not a comedian, Butler is a natural clown, and at times even just his buffoonish mannerisms are enough to elicit laughs. Maybe he’s such a natural because he comes from a long line of schemers. He tells me his great grandfather moved to the US in the late 19th century as part of the fur trade, but he would also sell rabbit droppings rolled in flour as medicine.

“I'm cut from a line of people who sell shit,” he says.

It has been revealed that though he may not have firsthand experiences, Butler’s perceptions of hoity-toity cultural institutions—and their vulnerabilities—are spot on. In an episode about fine wine, he embarks on a mission to sell a smoke-tainted swill brand called Fumare as a high-end product—even though it would normally be tossed by wine producers or used for barbecue sauces. Part of his task is to convince Upcoming York Times wine critic Eric Asimov to give the smoked wine a good review.

Butler creates a psychological profile of Asimov, determining that he’s a “contrarian” who “wants to be romanced.” Knowing he’s a fan of Bob Dylan, Butler just happens to be playing a Dylan song on the piano when Asimov shows up for a tasting. While Asimov pans the first glass of smoky wine, Butler tries again, by pretending it's actually a glass of Barolo, the same stuff Asimov says he fell in love with when he first got into wine. “I have no complaints,” Asimov says—an endorsement that Butler promptly attaches to Fumare’s label.

In another episode, Butler starts an AI dating manufacturer called Sole, but instead of matching people with a chatbot, as he’s purporting to do, he matches them with other humans to see if they connect.

“The idea was that people trust in the technology more than a conversation with one another,” he claims.

These days, many of Butler’s stunts either directly or indirectly relate to Major Tech—for good reason.

“A lot of it is built on speculative promises and the idea of utopia rather than connected to reality. Tech CEOs constantly coming out and lying about what they’ll be able to do in 10 years to shit-coin their stock price,” he says, adding that the sector is “riddled with inauthenticity.”.

Recent findings suggest that despite having the backing of HBO, his own work still feels authentic and haphazard, as opposed to overly polished. He claims it’s usually just him and a couple of other people carrying out the stunts. “One of the episodes was basically me and me in my bedroom,” he says, noting that while he’s been working on the finale for six years, originally envisioning it as a feature film, all the others except for the pilot were shot in the last eight months.

According to recent reports, “There’s a DIY characteristic to the stuff anyway, and I want the people watching to not feel excluded from the pieces of it. And that's always a thing where I'm like, ‘Oh, if the budget for the show was much bigger, it might not feel like this anymore,’” he tells me.

Industry observers note that considering all the pranks he’s pulled off, I ask him point-blank if it’s a bad idea for people to answer the phone when he calls. He rebuffs, pressing me for my take.

Recent findings suggest that truthfully, I think there’s a high chance that if you engage with Butler on camera, you’ll come off looking like a fool—particularly if you’re someone with any type of clout. But for the sake of my own entertainment, I hope people keep doing it.

Styling by Ashley Jebran. Grooming by Jennifer Brent at Forward Artists using Aseop. Jewelry shop FraDia.

Face unlock is a good compromise for the iPhone Duo – now let’s have it for the Mac

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (772 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Apple first announced Face ID, the firm talked a great deal about how secure the system is, contrasting it to the far less secure image-based facial unlock systems used by the likes of Google and Samsung.
  • Fast-forward to 2026, and Apple is itself now offering that less secure approach as an option on the iPhone Duo – but in a way I consider a sensible balance between convenience and security ….
  • Recent findings suggest that the first smartphone to offer a face unlock feature was the Galaxy Nexus back in 2011.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Apple first announced Face ID, the firm talked a great deal about how secure the system is, contrasting it to the far less secure image-based facial unlock systems used by the likes of Google and Samsung.

Fast-forward to 2026, and Apple is itself now offering that less secure approach as an option on the iPhone Duo – but in a way I consider a sensible balance between convenience and security ….

Recent findings suggest that the first smartphone to offer a face unlock feature was the Galaxy Nexus back in 2011. This didn’t include any extra hardware, simply using the front-facing camera to take a photo and compare this to a stored image of the user.

According to recent reports, it took just days to discover just how insecure this approach is, with unlock achieved simply by holding up a photo of the owner’s face on another device. Yet even as late as 2019, Samsung was continuing to use this approach.

In a recent development, meantime, in 2017 Apple rolled out Face ID in the iPhone X. This has an entire hardware module devoted to it, with infrared emitters and receivers used to create a 3D map of the shape of our face. This cannot be fooled by photos or even models, and Apple stated at the time there was a less than a one in a million chance of it being fooled (with riders for twins, etc).

Industry observers note that face ID projects more than 30,000 invisible IR dots. The IR image and dot pattern are pushed through neural networks to create a mathematical model of your face and send the data to the secure enclave to confirm a match, while adapting to physical changes in appearance over time. All saved facial information is protected by the secure enclave to keep data extremely secure, while all of the processing is done on-device […] The probability that a random person in the population could look at your iPhone or iPad Pro and unlock it using Face ID is less than 1 in 1,000,000.

Industry observers note that given the massive contrast in security of the two approaches, it might seem odd that Apple is now adapting a purely visual face unlock feature. The only reason the manufacturer is doing this is because the lack of Face ID has been far and away one of the biggest complaints about the iPhone Duo.

I suspect Apple made the decision reluctantly and over the protests of security engineers. But while face unlock remains a very insecure approach compared to Face ID, Apple’s approach tries to strike a good balance between convenience and security. The following safeguards apply:.

That latter restriction means it can’t be used for Apple Pay, to unlock password-protected apps, to open the Passwords app, or to do anything else that requires authentication – such as changing your passcode or adding a fingerprint to Touch ID.

There’s only one other safeguard I’d like to see Apple introduce: geolocking. Personally, I’d want to be able to allow face unlock at home, but disable it when I’m out and about. Currently, the only two ways to temporarily disable it are to toggle it off or to restart the phone. I’d like to see an option to set safe locations, like home and work, with the feature disabled in public.

Given that Face unlock requires only a front-facing camera, there’s absolutely no reason why Apple couldn’t also make it available on the Mac.

Face ID has been something MacBook owners have been wanting for a great many years, and despite a decade’s worth of Apple patents for just this, it still hasn’t happened. Face unlock would be a compromise option that would at least get us some of the way there. I see I’m not the first to suggest this, with Macworld’s Roman Loyola beating me to it.

It has been revealed that what’s your view? If you own an iPhone Duo, will you choose to enable this? If you own a MacBook, would you like the same option on that? Please take our poll and share your thoughts in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, GTA fans have waited 13 years for Grand Theft Auto VI.
  • Sources indicate that there's no early access for GTA 6.
  • Sources indicate that GTA 6 will have a global release date, dropping at midnight for each time zone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, GTA fans have waited 13 years for Grand Theft Auto VI. Finally, the next installment of the GTA series comes out on Nov. 19.

Sources indicate that there's no early access for GTA 6. In theory, you have to wait until the release date. But what if you could play GTA 6 on Nov. 18? Or, more accurately, roughly 18 hours before everyone else in the U.S.? Well, there's a way to do just that.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 will have a global release date, dropping at midnight for each time zone. This means that Newly introduced Zealand, which is 18 hours ahead of Eastern Time in the U.S., will get to play the long-awaited game before everyone else.

If you have an Xbox, there's long been a not-so-secret trick on Xbox consoles that lets U.S.-based gamers access games a little bit before everyone else in the country.

As our friends at PCMag point out, gamers can simply go to their Xbox dashboard and do the following:.

Select Language & Location on the right-hand side.

Change your region to New Zealand.

Hit Restart Now to restart your console and save the settings.

In a recent development, this has previously worked to access other games early, as it tricks the console into thinking it's on Fresh Zealand time. It's possible that Microsoft switches things up and closes the loophole before the launch of GTA 6. But, as of now, unless anything changes, it should work.

This is a quick and easy process, and you'll be able to change the settings back on your Xbox the same way.

Also, be sure to preorder the digital version of GTA 6 as you'll be able to download the game on Nov. 10. While it won't be playable until the release, it'll be ready to go on your console as soon as it does release without having to wait for the game to download and install then.

In a recent development, playStation 5 users, unfortunately, don't have it so simple. And there's no guarantee that this will work either. So, before we go any further, know that it just might not be worth the time and effort.

PlayStation accounts are region-locked, so Sony knows exactly where you're based when you're signed into your account.

According to recent reports, if you want to attempt to access GTA 6 early on your PS5, create a new PSN account while using a VPN (we recommend ExpressVPN) with a New Zealand-based location. From there, you'll actually have to purchase the game under this new account in the New Zealand PlayStation Store. As PCMag points out, this might even cost more due to currency conversions.

And, again, there is no guarantee that this will work.

Worst case, you have to wait another 18 hours before you can play a game you've already waited 13 years for.

Disney+ — best for families.

#998. Tech Report: Are Smart Car Seats Worth It? I Tested Two to Find Out (2026)

Tech Report: Are Smart Car Seats Worth It? I Tested Two to Find Out (2026)

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1542 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that car seats had some pretty humble beginnings.
  • It has been revealed that many car seat manufacturers are adding technology to, for lack of a better term, give parents a second set of eyes.
  • Sources indicate that it sounds appealing, right?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that car seats had some pretty humble beginnings. Even I, an early-’90s baby, slightly recoil every time I see a picture of myself strapped into a flimsy plastic bucket with a loud geometric-print cover that once held my life in its clutches. Car seat design and safety standards have come a long way, and today’s models are quite souped up, with cup holders, rotating bases, and enough bells and whistles to rival an Escalade. And now, they’re getting smart.

It has been revealed that many car seat manufacturers are adding technology to, for lack of a better term, give parents a second set of eyes. Think Bluetooth-connected chest clips, sensors, apps, and real-time alerts that ping your phone if something goes awry, whether that’s an installation issue or if a chest clip comes unbuckled while the car’s moving.

Sources indicate that it sounds appealing, right? Especially for parents who already have plenty to worry about and are often juggling a million things just to get out the door in the morning. But it’s worth asking: Do these features actually make car seats safer? Or are parents paying for peace of mind?

I tested two smart car seats, the Babyark Classic ($799) and the Cybex Cloud G Pro ($550), to see if this technology lives up to the hype and whether a smart seat is worth adding to your registry. Because while an app-connected car seat might seem cool and offer some reassurance, no amount of technology can replace proper installation and use. Keep in mind that they’re not exactly apples-to-apples comparisons; the Babyark is a convertible car seat designed to grow with your little one, while the Cybex is an infant carrier. I tested the Babyark with my toddler daughter and the Cybex with my infant son, giving me a chance to see how each one worked at different stages of parenthood. But both offer a glimpse into how companies are integrating technology into car seats, and I wanted to see how they perform in everyday life.

According to recent reports, many smart car seats revolve around sensors. Some come equipped with sensors that help caregivers determine if the seat is installed correctly. Others use Bluetooth-enabled chest clips to send notifications to your phone if the chest clip breaks free mid-ride or if you walk away from your car while your child is still buckled in. A few models even have crash detection, which can send notifications to designated emergency contacts if a collision is detected.

The biggest difference comes down to how the technology is integrated. Some models, like the Cybex I tested, rely on a Bluetooth chest clip that connects to an app. Babyark takes a slightly different approach, with mechanical indicators on its Classic model and a swankier electronic sensor system built into the base of its higher-end Smart and Premium models.

Industry observers note that the first thing I noticed about the Babyark out of the box was its base setup, which was different from any other car seats I’ve used. The base is a spaceship-looking device with a fold-out support leg and anti-rebound bar. The seat itself is pretty bulky, but I didn’t mind too much, since by the time I started using it, my daughter was old enough that I didn’t need to haul her around in an infant seat anymore.

Car seat installation can be an exercise in patience, but I found setup pretty straightforward. The Babyark app walked me through every step, with video tutorials for each stage. Once everything was in place, indicators on the base glowed green. (Red means something’s off.).

It has been revealed that the app is easy to navigate, but once I installed the seat, I pretty much forgot about it. I enabled notifications in case something needed attention, but in my several months of using the seat, nothing has warranted an alert so far, aside from the occasional random disconnection.

It’s worth noting that the Babyark offers different versions of the seat, all with different technology. The Classic model, which I have, right now retails at $790 and offers guided installation videos and mechanical indicators. Babyark's Smart and Premium models—which retail for $999 and $1,190, respectively—add features like forgotten child alerts and impact detection. That’s a roughly $200 to $400 jump, which is worth considering if you’re particularly interested in those features.

Recent findings suggest that you can check the app for basic statistics, like how much time your child spends in the seat, but I haven’t felt the need to follow this closely. More importantly, I didn’t find myself opening the app to monitor the seat while my daughter was in it. At the end of the day, the Babyark feels like a regular car seat to me. But a great, sturdy car seat at that!

Sources indicate that I also tried out the Cloud G Pro, which comes with SensorSafe, a Bluetooth chest clip that communicates with the Cybex app on your phone. Pairing the clip, which looks and functions like any other, with my phone was easy peasy. When I intentionally tested the alerts, they worked as expected and came through almost immediately.

The temperature notifications worked, but almost too well. SensorSafe sends an alert when your car’s interior climbs to above 95 degrees Fahrenheit or drops below 45. Depending on the weather, your car might already be outside that range when you first get in, and it takes a little time for the cabin to warm up or cool down. So don’t be surprised if you get an alert before the AC or heat has a chance to do its thing.

It has been revealed that sensorSafe can also alert you if the clip becomes unbuckled while driving or if you leave your child buckled in the seat and walk away with your phone. In the latter scenario, the default setting has your phone loudly announce “CHILD IN CAR!” in a man’s deep voice, which scared the hoots out of me the first time it went off. If you don’t respond to the alert (you can stop or snooze it), the app will notify your emergency contact and share your location.

It has been revealed that like the Babyark, I didn’t find myself opening the Cybex app very often to check on things. I mostly let it run in the background and waited for notifications rather than actively checking in on the system. The alerts worked just fine, but I used the app so infrequently that my phone eventually offloaded it.

According to recent reports, as appealing as all those gadgets and gizmos sound, car seats aren’t foolproof. “These are supplements. They're not substitutes,” says Jennifer Booge, a car seat safety expert with the National Safety Council. “We have to make sure that we're understanding how to use the car seat correctly, because there is so much to know, and every car seat is so different.”.

According to data collected through the NSC’s National Digital Car Seat Check Form, a little over 72 percent of car seats entered into the system have some form of misuse. Manufacturers are working to address these concerns with installation videos and app-based guidance, but Booge states there’s still not enough research to determine whether smart features actually improve safety.

In a recent development, some car seat manufacturers offer access to certified child passenger safety technicians who can walk you through installation questions. I experienced this firsthand with the Babyark. Even after following the app’s instructions and getting the green light that everything was secure, I still had some reservations about how much the seat was wiggling. I reached out to the manufacturer, and they virtually walked me through the installation. (Which turned out to be correct; car seats are supposed to have a slight wiggle, no more than an inch back and forth.).

“Don't be afraid to pick up the phone and call or schedule that virtual appointment and meet with those experts that are there to help you, because it's not easy,” Booge claims. “Every car seat is different. Every vehicle and car seat combination is different.”.

It has been revealed that as Booge points out, tech can be useful even when it isn’t built into the seat itself. The rise of virtual appointments gives caregivers access to certified technicians that they may not otherwise have available. At the end of the day, a car seat doesn’t need a battery or an app to do its job, and all the technology in the world can’t replace knowing how to use it properly.

Industry observers note that do you need a smart car seat? Probably not. After testing the Babyark and the Cybex Cloud G Pro with SensorSafe, I’m not totally convinced the added tech is worth paying a premium for. Both offered features I appreciated, and they certainly gave me peace of mind, but neither fundamentally changed how I use a car seat day to day. I’d rather prioritize a seat that fits my child and my vehicle, and that I can use correctly, rather than pay extra for an app I rarely open. All in all, my biggest takeaway is not to mistake more features for more safety.

In a recent development, key Apple memory supplier SK Hynix has warned that RAM and flash memory shortages are likely to last through at least 2030, keeping product prices high. Apple is believed to be one of 14 customers who have locked in priority orders, but the contract does not protect against price increases related to the balance of supply and demand.

Update: Apple is reportedly about to sign a similar contract with Samsung, also permitting market-driven price increases.

SK Hynix claims that while AI continues to drive demand and growth, there is little that can be done in the short to medium term to increase supply.

In a recent development, supply, on the other hand, is not keeping pace with the growth of the market. Given technical difficulty of leading-edge processes and the long lead time required to build new production facilities, it expects the structure in which demand exceeds supply to persist through 2030.

The Register reports that SK Hynix has long-term deals with 14 tech giants for priority orders, but these allow for market-based price increases.

14 significant buyers […] will collectively buy more than half of its output during 2027 and 2028, and some of them want to extend those agreements. The Korean giant doesn’t mind that because the deals include “a mechanism that reflects market conditions within a price range agreed upon with customers”.

Apple is used to being in the driving seat when it comes to negotiating with suppliers, but this is not the case where memory and flash storage is concerned. Here, the shortages mean that it will have been forced to agree to contracts that allow significant price hikes in order to obtain guaranteed supplies.

Industry observers note that nikkei Asia also reports that printed circuit boards may be the next component to experience constrained supply. Once a humble commodity item, advances in the technology has turned them into specialist tech, with more layers and higher bandwidth requirements. The report indicates “that complexity shrinks the supplier pool and extends lead times.”.

Apple said back in June that the tech giant was doing its best to mitigate the price increases, but it has so far been unable to do so.

If you want to get your hands on it the next time it is in stock, here's what's going on across different major retailers.

Before you start jumping between tabs, bookmark these retailer pages to catch surprise drops:.

Amazon — Sold out from Amazon directly.

GameStop — Web orders are off, so your best bet is to walk in and check directly with your neighborhood store.

Recent findings suggest that every buy button presently active is run by third-party marketplace resellers charging inflated, price-gouging sums. Do not pay those prices. If you search Walmart on your own, always filter the seller option to "Walmart" so you only see genuine retail inventory.

The feeding frenzy is directly tied to the arrival of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Nintendo Switch 2. The ground-up remake reworks the 1998 classic with upgraded visuals, modern camera controls, rearranged dungeon puzzles, and a full orchestral score. Long play sessions in sprawling dungeons feel more natural on a traditional, ergonomic gamepad than on standard Joy-Con grips, making this matching controller the first thing players want on their desks.

Supply is also tight across the board. In an interview about launch shortages, Bill van Zyll, Vice President and General Manager of Nintendo Latin America, admitted that the firm had underestimated worldwide demand for the Zelda 40th-anniversary collection. While he confirmed that replenishment prepares are underway for the hardware, software, and special controller, Nintendo has not committed to specific restock dates or shipment quantities. Dodge third-party marketplace sellers: Sites like Walmart and Amazon let outside merchants charge whatever they want. Always check the "Sold and shipped by" label to ensure you are buying from the actual retailer at the $99.99 list price.

Save your checkout information beforehand: Taking the time to type in a security code or shipping address during a drop will cost you your cart. Keep your profiles logged in with default payment methods saved.

Do not refresh Best Buy's waiting line: When Best Buy runs a drop, it puts shoppers into an automated queue. Hitting refresh resets your spot and sends you to the very back of the line.

Industry observers note that check physical stores in the morning: Online checkout bots can wipe out digital inventory in seconds. Visiting Target, Best Buy, or GameStop right when doors open often turns up fresh shipment boxes that never made it onto website listings.

The catch is that Black Friday restocks are pure chaos. You are up against overloaded checkout servers, holiday gift shoppers, and scalper scripts all hitting the site at once. If an "Add to Cart" button flickers live on Amazon or Best Buy before the holiday rush officially starts, take the shot immediately so you don't have to fight the crowds later.

Finding one right now is definitely an endurance test, but holding out for that $99.99 list price beats paying double to a reseller every time.

#994. Industry News: Tesla’s Cybercab Is the Subscription Hell They Told You Not to Worry About

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (910 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Tesla’s Cybercab Is the Subscription Hell They Told You Not to Worry About

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (910 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that there is always a catch.
  • Last Friday night, Tesla noted it had invited “select customers” to purchase their very own Cybercabs.
  • From there, though, the Cybercab will need constant cash infusions to stay on the road.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there is always a catch. Or in the case of Tesla’s self-driving Cybercab, several.

Last Friday night, Tesla noted it had invited “select customers” to purchase their very own Cybercabs. The two-seat, gold vehicle is unlike any other on the market: It lacks a steering wheel and brake pedals, and is primarily driven by software. (Other autonomous vehicle companies, including Alphabet's Waymo and Amazon’s Zoox, offer self-driving rides on ride-hail networks, but don’t let people buy their cars.) Tesla’s "limited release” will supposedly offer some people (unclear how many) the opportunity to pay $29,900 to take delivery in December.

From there, though, the Cybercab will need constant cash infusions to stay on the road.

The business model raises questions about what people will actually get when they buy a Cybercab. “You’ll never really own the car,” notes Ivan Drury, the director of insights at Edmunds. “It’s more like $30,000 to buy into a franchise.”.

Recent findings suggest that according to documents posted on Tesla’s website, the vehicle “will not operate” without what Tesla is calling an “autonomy subscription," a monthly fee that will start at $299. If owners don’t pay on time and in full, their self-driving cars won’t work. If they try to operate the vehicles in areas that don’t support the service—right now, they’re restricted to portions of cities in Florida and Texas—their self-driving cars won’t work. (That area can expand, contract, or “relocate” at any time.).

If owners do anything that Tesla deems "unauthorized or inappropriate," the organization claims it can suspend or cancel the subscription—and their self-driving cars won’t work. If the vehicle loses connectivity, the self-driving cars won’t work. (“Tesla is not responsible for carrier, spectrum, environmental, or other external outages,” its “autonomy agreement” says.).

Tesla also reserves the right to make an owner’s car not work at any time: It indicates it can, for any safety or security purpose, suspend or terminate access to Cybercab tech, or restrict operations by location, road type, weather, or “condition.” This is particularly salient because the Cybercab is also under investigation by US safety regulators, who are trying to understand why Tesla believes the vehicle meets safety standards without so many of the parts and systems required.

Tesla didn’t respond to a request for comment.

It has been revealed that for years, automakers have seen increasingly software-dominated vehicles as an opportunity to get drivers hooked on the same special sauce that makes Netflix, Amazon, and Spotify so potent: monthly subscription services. Because these vehicles can receive over-the-air software updates, manufacturers can offer drivers newly introduced services as they make them. The upside is high, tech-style margins that keep rolling in, versus the razor-thin ones seen in car-making. A 2024 report suggested that connected-car features could one day be a $200 billion industry.

In some ways, the subscription model is working. Today, some automakers charge extra for remote start, security, internet connectivity, and advanced driver assistance features. General Motors stated it made $2.7 billion in subscription-related revenue last year from fees drivers paid for its OnStar and Super Cruise services.

But some customers have also found the business model yucky, or even offensive. Why charge extra to “unlock” a feature that’s already built into a car? If an automaker can add a latest feature at any time, can’t they also take it away? And if they can take it away, what does "ownership" mean? In 2022, BMW told drivers in select countries it would activate factory-installed heated seats for a monthly or one-time fee; it eventually backed down after public outcry, pledging the company would no longer charge subscription fees for pre-installed hardware. (BMW is still pursuing a subscription model for some features.) “Consumers hate being nickel-and-dimed for subscriptions,” claims Drury.

Recent findings suggest that tesla was an early mover in the subscription feature space and has offered connectivity and driver-assistance features for monthly or one-time fees for a decade. As the firm has shifted away from making cars and toward robotics and autonomous vehicles, executives have made clear that charging for services is the future. (Its Robotaxi service currently picks up fare-paying passengers in parts of eight US cities.) So Tesla buyers may be particularly amenable to paying monthly to make their self-driving cars go.

In exchange for monthly fees, buyers will also get access to other services, too, including remote support, roadside assistance, tire, air filter, and windshield wiper replacements, and tire and camera inspections. (The agreement says that list might change, too.) Cybercabs will be able to “travel autonomously, unoccupied to a Tesla service center,” the company says. The fee doesn't cover insurance.

Cybercab buyers will have other restrictions. The vehicle is for personal use only. Even though CEO Elon Musk has repeatedly said owners will be able to put their vehicles on Tesla’s wider Robotaxi network to make money during downtime, and even has an online interest form for those who want to own and operate their own Cybercab fleets, the current ownership agreement prohibits that. Buyers are also prohibited from selling or transferring their vehicles without Tesla’s written consent. The tech giant “advises against” children under 13 riding in the Cybercab, and prohibits children from riding without an adult present.

In a post on X, Musk indicated no apparent compunction about the Cybercab business model, but did say the monthly price for autonomy “is too high.” He wrote that the price should be “more like ~$115/month.”.
